EXPECTED FAILURE

Ordarium `InvalidCursorError`, whose stable `code` is the string `"INVALID_CURSOR"` (an `OrdariumError` subclass; message: "The change cursor is not a valid durable position; refusing to guess a resume point").

This is the failure for a rejected *stored observation cursor*: Ordarium's state kind exposes `StateChangeFeed.changes(filter, cursor)` as "incremental observation of committed state revisions after a durable position" (ORD-BOOT-0), and `StateChangePage.cursor` is the always-present "durable resume position" a consumer stores and replays. A replayed cursor is rejected, fail-closed, in two cases:
  1. it is not decodable as base64url of `{"c":"<digits>"}`, or
  2. it decodes but its position exceeds the ledger's global change high-water mark (a restored/replaced ledger lowered the mark).
Both paths throw `InvalidCursorError`, deliberately distinct from `LedgerCorruptError`: invalid caller input, not damaged ledger content, and it refuses to silently restart the feed from the beginning. It is also not retry-safe: unlike `StateRevisionConflictError` (busy family), replaying the same rejected cursor cannot succeed.

WHY (source precedence)

`docs/engineering/08-source-precedence-policy.md` (PLMP-ALN-2) orders sources: (1) the published contract of the *exact pinned version* governs an interface; (2) the project's normative specification; (3) informational records are explanatory only and "never override 1 or 2."

The pinned dependency is @ordarium/core / @ordarium/ledger-sqlite **1.3.1** (`package.json:32-34`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml:15-18`; installed `node_modules/@ordarium/{core,ledger-sqlite}/package.json` both report 1.3.1). Its shipped declarations are therefore the governing source (rule 1):
  - `node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/errors.d.ts` (InvalidCursorError doc) and `errors.js:161-164` define the class and `code: "INVALID_CURSOR"`.
  - `node_modules/@ordarium/core/dist/src/types.d.ts:160-177` / `state.d.ts:28` define the observation feed and its always-present durable cursor.
  - `node_modules/@ordarium/ledger-sqlite/dist/src/index.js:386-394` (high-water rejection) and `:770-790` (decode rejection) throw it; `capabilities.stateChangeFeed = true`.

The only workspace source asserting a different identity is `docs/engineering/notes/error-code-note.md`, which says the failure was "historically ... numeric code 27" and is explicitly marked "informational, not normative." Under rule 3 it cannot override the pinned contract. Even the in-force alignment record, `docs/engineering/07-ordarium-alignment.md:38,53`, assigns the 27–29 numeric range to STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT / STATE_REF_NOT_FOUND and mandates mapping errors by `instanceof`, not by numeric code — so no local normative source supports "27 = cursor rejection" either.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE INTEGRATION

Branch on `error instanceof InvalidCursorError` (fallback `error.code === "INVALID_CURSOR"`), and surface it as a hard, fail-closed input error. Do not route it into the transient/busy family, do not hardcode 27, and do not treat it as `StateRevisionConflictError` (STATE_REVISION_CONFLICT). Scope note: the pinned contract is the authority regardless of the installed version's owner; the current telemetry state integration (`src/telemetry/state_persistence.ts`) still loads through `store.list()` pagination and does not yet call `changes()`, so this failure is reached once that integration stores/reuses an observation (change-feed) cursor.
